about.title: Medicine, practiced with precision and presence

blogPosts.title: Understanding IVF Success Rates: What the Numbers Actually Mean
blogPosts.excerpt: Success rates get quoted constantly in fertility care — here's how to actually read them for your situation.
blogPosts.author: Dr. Aparna Rao
content: Published IVF success rates are almost always reported as clinic averages across all ages and diagnoses — which makes them close to meaningless for any individual patient.
The number that actually matters is your projected success rate, based on your age, ovarian reserve, and specific diagnosis, which your fertility specialist calculates during your initial workup.
Ask your clinic for their live-birth rate per embryo transfer for your age bracket specifically — that's the number with real predictive value.

Success also compounds across cycles. A 35% per-cycle rate can mean a much higher cumulative chance of success across two or three cycles, which is part of why treatment planning looks further ahead than one attempt.
